title: Check If N and Its Double Exist
statement: Decide whether `arr` holds a value that is exactly twice another value stored at a **different** position. In other words, look for indices `i` and `j` with `i != j` and `arr[i] == 2 * arr[j]`. Return `true` when such a pair of indices exists and `false` when it does not.
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every ordered pair of positions answers the question in O(n²). Instead, walk the array once and remember every value already passed in a set. For each new value there are only two partners that would complete a pair: its double (the new value is the smaller one) or its half (the new value is the larger one). Two set lookups settle both.

## Approach

1. Create an empty set `seen`.
2. For each `value` of `arr`, check whether `value * 2` is already in `seen`; if so, return `true`.
3. If `value` is even, also check for `value / 2` in `seen`; if found, return `true`.
4. Add `value` to `seen` and continue.
5. If the loop ends without a match, return `false`.

Because a value is added only after its own checks, a single `0` never pairs with itself, but a second `0` finds the first.

## Example 1, step by step

`arr = [10, 2, 5, 3]`.

- `10`: `seen` is empty, so no match; `seen = {10}`.
- `2`: `4` and `1` are not in `seen`; `seen = {10, 2}`.
- `5`: `10` is in `seen`, so return `true` (10 is twice 5).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant-time set lookups.
- Space: O(n): the set may hold every value.

## Pitfalls

- Zero is its own double, so a `0` only counts when a second `0` exists; adding `value` before its checks would wrongly pair a lone zero with itself.
- Check both directions: the double may appear before or after its half.
- Only look for a half when `value` is even; `value / 2` of an odd number is a fraction that can never match, and with negatives `value % 2` is `-1`, not `1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | the values visited so far |
| `value` | the current element of `arr` |

narration.2: Start with an empty set of the values visited so far.
narration.4: Visit the values from left to right.
narration.5: If the double of this value was already seen, this value is the half of a pair.
narration.6: A pair at two different positions exists, so answer true.
narration.8: For an even value, its half may have been seen earlier, making this value the double.
narration.9: That is also a valid pair, so answer true.
narration.11: Remember this value only after checking it, so a value never pairs with itself.
narration.13: No value had a partner, so no such pair exists.
